instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.

Cut half the ciabatta loaf (about 8 oz) into 1 inch cubes. Bread that's a day or two old works best. Spread the cubes on the sheet, drizzle them with 1 tbsp olive oil, sprinkle on 1/4 tsp salt and toss them with your hands.
Bake for 7 to 10 minutes, until the edges are crisp and golden but the middles still give a little when you squeeze one. Leave them to cool on the sheet.
Meanwhile, grate the 2 garlic cloves into your biggest bowl. Add 4 tbsp olive oil, 3 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1/2 tsp Dijon, 1/2 tsp salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper, and whisk until it's smooth.
Cut the 1.5 lbs tomatoes into wedges and slice half the cucumber into half moons. Thinly slice half the red onion.
Add the tomatoes, cucumber, onion and toasted bread to the dressing and toss until everything is coated.
Tear in about 1 cup of the basil leaves and toss gently. Leave it for 10 minutes and toss it once or twice, so the bread softens a little in the tomato juices.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a splash more of the vinegar.
Serve with a few more basil leaves torn over the top.
method_notes: All three toast cubes or torn pieces of crusty bread in the oven with a little olive oil, then toss them with tomatoes, cucumber and basil in a mustard and red wine vinegar dressing. Love and Lemons (the lead) bakes the bread at 350°F until crisp at the edges, adds red onion and three grated garlic cloves to the dressing, and makes mozzarella optional. RecipeTin Eats salts the tomatoes in a colander first and whisks their juice into the dressing, and rests the salad 5 minutes. Spend With Pennies toasts the bread hotter, at 425°F, adds parsley and rests it 15 minutes. This one uses the lead's amounts as a lunch for 4, with two garlic cloves and a 10 minute rest.
